finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST handler passes the raw `feed` POST parameter to file_get_contents, allowing SSRF to arbitrary URLs and local file reads via stream wrappers (file://, php://) when allow_url_fopen is enabled.

trace.note: session_start() runs but no auth check is applied to this branch
Branch taken for any POST containing a 'feed' field
Attacker-controlled value passed directly to file_get_contents
strlen of fetched body echoed back, giving the attacker a length oracle

finding.guards_checked: None on the path: no scheme allowlist, no host/IP allowlist or private-range denylist, no DNS pinning, no redirect control. Authentication is absent. allow_url_fopen is set in php.ini outside this repo and was not verified.

verdict.guard_found: none. import.php:2 only calls session_start(). The feed branch at import.php:11 is checked before and independently of require_admin() (defined at import.php:4-9, called only at import.php:18 for set_webhook). No scheme, host, or IP check exists between line 11 and the sink at line 12. The length oracle at line 13 matches the candidate's description.
verdict.reason: Any remote POST with a `feed` field reaches file_get_contents($_POST['feed']) at import.php:12 without authentication or validation, since the branch at import.php:11 returns before the admin check at line 18. The allow_url_fopen precondition is outside the repo and was not verified, so the SSRF and file-read impact depends on that php.ini setting, but the code path itself is attacker-reachable and unguarded.
